chunks: A part of it: In the description of the Angels (peace be upon them)

Then He, the Glorified, created for the inhabiting of His skies and the populating of the highest stratum of His realm, a wondrous creation from His angels. With them He filled the openings of its cavities, and with them He populated the vastness of its atmosphere. Between the openings of these cavities resounds the chanting of those among them who glorify Him in the enclosures of Holiness, behind the curtains of concealment, and in the pavilions of Glory. And behind this resounding, which deafens the ears, are the clouds of light that restrain the eyes from reaching it, so they stand disappointed at their limits. He created them in different shapes and with diverse capacities, (those possessing wings) who glorify the Sublimity of His Honour. They do not appropriate to themselves the skill that appears in creation, nor do they claim that they create anything with Him from that which He is unique in. 'But they are rather honoured servants. They do not take precedence over Him in uttering anything, and they act according to His command.'
ai.seo_question: What is the theological description of the angels' creation and role in the universe according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In the chapter of Al-Ashbaah, Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the ontological hierarchy of the angels as distinct creations designed to populate the celestial spheres, emphasizing their pure servitude without self-will. This description aligns with the Shia theological understanding of angels as luminous beings who execute divine commands flawlessly, serving as a bridge between the unseen and the material world. The passage underscores their continuous glorification and lack of speech unless commanded, reinforcing their role as honored servants who reflect God's majesty.
